signals.title: USD/NOK — G10 Bilateral Theme + Fed Divergence
signals.text: The G10 scorecard shows USD leading performance with a 1W average of +1.041% across 9 pairs, while NOK lags at −1.001% across 2 pairs, generating an extreme bilateral spread of 2.042%. The divergence is fundamentally anchored by Fed policy after delivering a 25bp hike to 4.00% against Norges Bank on hold at 4.25%, with the US yield curve reinforcing policy strength in a bear flattener regime as 2s10s sits at +33.6bp. Spot trades at 9.426, holding above the SMA20 at 9.308 while remaining below the SMA50/200 cluster at 9.465/9.594. Retail positioning is one-sided at 91% long USD/NOK, presenting overhead positioning drag even as macro divergence accelerates. Trade bias: Long USD/NOK, underpinned by policy divergence and G10 momentum spread. Catalyst: Norges Bank policy decision 24 Sep. Risk: Brent crude rebound above $105/bbl that cushions NOK terms of trade and compresses the spread below 0.80%.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Crowded Long Positioning
signals.text: CFTC data shows Leveraged Funds net long AUD at +48,379 contracts, placing positioning at the 93rd percentile and +1.72 standard deviations of its 52-week historical distribution. This crowded spec long profile coincides with a WoW reduction of −1,871 contracts, signaling stall in accumulation. Spot trades at 0.7121, trapped between the SMA50 at 0.7080 and the SMA20 at 0.7170. Options markets reflect caution, with 1M implied volatility running at 7.2% against realized HV30 of 5.4%, generating an elevated vol risk premium of +1.8% alongside a mild −0.72 put skew. Trade bias: Neutral/range AUD/USD, crowded positioning limiting further upside extension. Catalyst: RBA policy meeting 29 Sep. Risk: Leveraged funds net positioning expanding above +55,000 contracts to drive a momentum breakout above 0.7170.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Tariff Risk + Technical Breakdown
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1486, failing to recover ground and holding firmly below its SMA20 (1.1616), SMA50 (1.1538), and SMA200 (1.1635) stack. Fundamental headwinds intensified following US announcements reviving trade tariffs on European trade ties, compounding a widening policy spread where Fed at 4.00% maintains a 135bp nominal carry advantage over ECB at 2.65% (+145bp on an OIS SOFR-€STR basis). ESI prints show European data beats moderating to +11.2 while Spain unemployment data showed a sharp increase. Leveraged positioning sits net short EUR at −46,381 contracts, reflecting institutional entrenchment against euro upside. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD, weighed down by trade frictions and policy divergence. Catalyst: Eurozone Final CPI release today at 09:00 UTC. Risk: Headline CPI printing above the 2.8% consensus, triggering ECB rate hike repricing.
evidence: Fed 4.0% vs ECB 2.65% — 135bp USD carry advantage

signals.title: USD/CHF — Options Volatility Disconnect
signals.text: USD/CHF 1M implied volatility sits at 6.5% against a 30-day realized volatility of 7.4%, producing an inverted vol risk premium of −0.9%. This pricing anomaly indicates severe options market complacency relative to actual spot movement. Spot trades at 0.8238, holding firmly above its SMA20 (0.8094), SMA50 (0.8101), and SMA200 (0.7936) baseline, reinforced by an immense 400bp Fed-SNB nominal policy differential (Fed 4.00% vs SNB 0.00%). Leveraged funds maintain net short CHF at −13,968 contracts in the 12th percentile of historical positioning, confirming deep structural funding status. Trade bias: Long USD/CHF, supported by positive carry and low realized hedging costs. Catalyst: SNB policy decision 24 Sep. Risk: Broad cross-asset volatility spike taking VIX above 25.0, triggering rapid CHF funding unwind.
evidence: Fed 4.0% vs SNB 0.0% — 400bp USD carry advantage
